mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 3.5% over the prior 8 weeks reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past 8 weeks
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during a similar 8-week rate rise period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite the labor signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.2% suggests accelerating demand growth, which anticipates higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative despite sustained consumption growth (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below -1% indicates weakening supply-side constraints, which typically precedes a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as market anticipates inventory drawdowns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 1% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when INDPRO contracts by >1% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in the federal funds rate turns positive (FEDFUNDS up), it indicates tightening, which reduces the discount rate applied to equities and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during prior months of rate increases (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% triggers a psychological shift in market expectations toward rate cuts, which drives a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 3.5% in a month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when UNRATE crosses the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (implied by HOUST) above 2% signal resilient consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative despite sustained retail sales growth (rolling IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained interaction between a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in new home sales (implied proxy via GDP dynamics) suggests easing supply constraints, which predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when INDPRO declines and GDPC1 rises simultaneously (p > 0.05).
